==Problem==

For his birthday, Bert gets a box that holds 125 jellybeans when filled to capacity. A few weeks later, Carrie gets a larger box full of jellybeans. Her box is twice as high, twice as wide and twice as long as Bert's. Approximately, how many jellybeans did Carrie get? 

<imath> \text{(A)}\ 250\qquad\text{(B)}\ 500\qquad\text{(C)}\ 625\qquad\text{(D)}\ 750\qquad\text{(E)}\ 1000 </imath>

==Solution==
Since each dimension of Carrie's box is twice the corresponding dimension of Bert's box, Carrie's box has <imath>2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 8</imath> times the volume of Bert's Box.  Therefore, Carrie's box can hold <imath>8\cdot125=\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 1000}</imath> jellybeans.
